newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-JUSKOWIAK DOUBLE KNOCKS ARSENAL OUT OF UEFA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUSKOWIAK DOUBLE KNOCKS ARSENAL OUT OF UEFA CUP.

text.p: Polish striker Andrzej Juskowiak scored twice in Borussia Moenchengladbach's 3-2 win over Arsenal which carried the German side into the second round of the UEFA Cup on Wednesday.
Arsenal, 3-2 down after the first leg of the first-round tie in England, turned in a battling performance but could not quite turn the match around.
Juskowiak gave Moenchengladbach a dream start with a 23rd-minute strike after a defence-splitting pass from captain Stefan Effenberg.
But Arsenal fought back with goals from Ian Wright and Paul Merson either side of the interval in a pulsating tie.

Effenberg, the German side's outstanding player, put Moenchengladbach level in the 75th minute with a well-placed shot but Arsenal continued to take the game to the home team, knowing one goal could take the match into extra-time.
Juskowiak took advantage of gaps in the Arsenal defence to hit his second in the 89th minute.
"Today we saw just how important Stefan Effenberg is for us," Moenchengladbach coach Bernd Krauss said. "Arsenal never gave up and when we went 2-1 behind, I thought it was going to be very tight."
"It was hard going," Effenberg said. "Arsenal played much better than they did in England but if you take both ties together, I think we deserve to go through."
